\label{MainThm}
		There exists $\eta > 0$ such that if
		$s \in (0,2)$ then there exists a probability measure $\nu$ supported on $\mathcal B$ with the following two properties:
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item \label{MainThm_point_Frostman_dimension} (Large Frostman dimension) 
			For any ball $I$ of radius 
			$r(I)$, we have
			\begin{equation}
				\label{Frostman}
				\nu(I) \ll_s r(I)^s.
			\end{equation}
			\item \label{MainThm_point_decay} (Polynomial Fourier decay)
			For any ${\boldsymbol{\xi}} \in \mathbb Z^2$, 
			we have
			\[
			\widehat \nu({\boldsymbol{\xi}}) \ll_\eta
			(1 + \| {\boldsymbol{\xi}} \|_\infty)^{-\eta}.
			\]
		\end{enumerate}

		(\log |\xi|)^{-A}

			\sum_{t=1}^\infty

\label{MDP}
		Let $F$ be a Borel subset of $\mathbb R^n$, for some $n \in \mathbb N$, and suppose $\mu$ is a Borel probability measure supported on $F$. Assume that, for some $\varepsilon >0 $ and some $s > 0$, we have
		\[
		\mu(U) \ll {\mathrm{diam}}(U)^s
		\]
		for all Borel sets $U$ such that ${\mathrm{diam}}(U) \leqslant \varepsilon$. Then
		\[
		\mathrm{dim}_{\mathrm{H}}(F) \geqslant s.
		\]

First of all, note that the left-hand side of \eqref{lem_ub_zero_result} is trivially  bounded above by $1$. 
Because of this, in the rest of the proof it is enough to consider parameters such that the right-hand side of~\eqref{lem_ub_zero_result} is strictly less than 1, that is 
\begin{equation} \label{rhs_is_small}
\frac{b}{|A|^{1/2} a^{3/2}} < \frac{1}{m} \cdot 
\end{equation}
Further, note that the right-hand side of~\eqref{lem_ub_zero_result} is decreasing with respect to the parameter $a$. So, without loss of generality, we can assume that
\begin{equation} \label{a_is_min_g}
a = \min \{ G(t): 0 \leqslant t \leqslant 1 \} = G(x_0)
\end{equation}
for some $x_0 \in [0,1].$ 

Define
\[
F(x) = f(x-B/A)  \qquad (B/A \leqslant x \leqslant 1+B/A).
\]
Then
\[
\int_X^Y e(f(t)) {\,{\rm d}} t =   \int_{X+B/A}^{Y+B/A} e(F(x)) {\,{\rm d}} x.
\]
We compute that
\[
F'(x) = A x G(x - B/A), \qquad
F''(x) = A G(x - B/A) + A x G'(x - B/A).
\]
Put $\mathcal I = [X+B/A, Y+B/A]$ and $c = a/(2b)$. For $|x| \leqslant c$, we have
\[
|F''(x)| \geqslant |A| (a - cb) = |A|a/2,
\]
and Lemma~\ref{lem_ub_nozero} 
yields
\[
\int_{\mathcal I \cap [-c,c]} e(F(x)) {\,{\rm d}} x \ll (|A| a)^{-1/2}.
\]

Next, decompose $\mathcal I \setminus [-c,c]$ into a disjoint union
\[
\mathcal I \setminus [-c,c] = \mathcal I_1 \cup \cdots \cup \mathcal I_{m+2}
\]
of intervals on which $F'$ is monotonic, and consider some 
$j \in [m+2]$.
For all $x\in \mathcal I \setminus 
[-c, c]$, we have
\[
|F'(x)| > |A|ca \gg |A|a^2/b.
\]
Now Lemma~\ref{lem_ub_nozero} yields
\[
\int_{\mathcal I_j} e(F(x))
\mathrm{d}x \ll \frac{b}{|A|a^2}.
\]
Combining the estimates above and applying~\eqref{rhs_is_small} and \eqref{a_less_than_b}, we conclude that 
\begin{align*}
\int_X^Y e(f(t)) {\,{\rm d}} t &\ll (|A|a)^{-1/2} + (m+2)\frac{b}{|A|a^{2}} \\ &\leqslant 
\Big(1 + \frac{m+2}{m}\Big) 
\frac{1}{|A|^{1/2} a^{1/2}} 
\ll \frac{mb}{|A|^{1/2} a^{3/2}}.
\end{align*}

Let $({\alpha},{\gamma}) \in \mathcal B_{M,R}$. Let $n\in \mathbb N$, and write
\[
n = \sum_{k=0}^K c_{k+1} q_k
\asymp q_K 
\]
for the Ostrowski expansion of $n$ with respect to ${\alpha}$. As in Lemma~\ref{nag}, we let $m \geqslant 0$ be minimal such that ${\delta}_{m+1} \ne 0,$ where ${\delta}_k$ is as in \eqref{delta_k_def}. Note from Lemma \ref{nag} that 
\[
\| n {\alpha} - {\gamma} \| = \min \{ |S|, 1-|S| \},
\]
where
\[
S = \sum_{k=m}^\infty {\delta}_{k+1} D_m.
\]
It therefore suffices to find lower bounds for $|S|$ and $1-|S|$. It follows from \cite[Lemma 4.4]{BHV} that there exists some 
$\ell \leqslant \max\{2, K-m + 1\}$ such that $|S| \geqslant |D_{m+\ell +1}|.$ Since $({\alpha},{\gamma}) \in \mathcal B_{M,R}$ implies that $m \leqslant K + R$, this gives
\[
|S| \geqslant |D_{m+1+\ell}| \gg 
\min \{ q_m^{-1}, q_K^{-1} \}
\gg q_K^{-1} \gg n^{-1}. 
\]
Regarding $1-|S|,$ it is shown in \cite[Lemma 4.5]{BHV} that for some positive integer $L \leqslant K+2$, 
\[ 
1 - |S| \geqslant |D_L| \gg q_L^{-1} \gg  n^{-1}.
\]
Combining, we deduce that 
\[
\| n {\alpha} - {\gamma} \| \gg n^{-1},
\]
where the implied constant depends at most on $M$ and $R$, whence  $\mathcal B_{M,R} \subseteq \mathcal B$.

\[
q_1 = a_1, \qquad q_2 = a_2 a_1 + 1
\]
and
\[
v_1 = a_1 - 1 \in [q_1/2,q_1],
\qquad
v_2 = a_2 (a_1 - 1) \in [q_2/3,q_2].
\]
Next, let $k \in [3,m] \cap \mathbb Z$, and assume that the result holds with $k$ replaced by $k-1$ or $k-2$. Then
\[
v_k \leqslant a_k v_{k-1} + v_{k-2} \leqslant a_k q_{k-1} + q_{k-2} = q_k.
\]
If $k \mmod R \notin \{0,1,2\}$ then
\[

\leqslant 3^{n_k} (a_k v_{k-1} + v_{k-2}) = 3^{n_k} v_k.
\]
If $k \mmod R \in \{0,1,2\}$ then
\[
q_k =  a_k q_{k-1} + q_{k-2} \leqslant (a_k + 1) q_{k-1} \leqslant 3^{n_k - 1} (a_k + 1) v_{k-1} \leqslant 3^{n_k} v_k.

\eqref{point_dimFrostman}  Fix $\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^2$ and $r>0.$ If $\nu(B_r(\mathbf x))=0$ then the claim is straightforward, so in the rest of the proof we assume that $\nu(B_r(\mathbf x))>0$. Define
\begin{equation} \label{def_Q0_N}
Q_0:=\exp(J_0 \sigma_m(\kappa)) \qquad \text{ and  } \qquad N:=\left\lfloor\frac{\log r}{-\log Q_0}\right\rfloor+1.
\end{equation}
These definitions imply  
\begin{equation} \label{r_level}
Q_0^{-N} < r \leqslant Q_0^{1-N}.
\end{equation}
Let $C=C(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$ be a cylinder set with $(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)\in\mathcal E^N$  such that
\begin{equation} \label{lem_FD_nontrivial_intersection}
\nu\left(B_r(\mathbf x)\cap C\right)>0.
\end{equation}
Setting  $J=J_0 N$ and $Q=\exp(J{\sigma}_m({\kappa}))=Q_0^N$ as above, point~\eqref{point_sizeQJ} of the lemma gives
\begin{equation} \label{lem_FD_size_q}
Q^{1-2\varepsilon}
\leqslant q_{J}(\mathbf a)\leqslant Q^{1+2\varepsilon}.
\end{equation}

We aim to provide an upper bound for the number of cylinder sets $C(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$, where $(\mathbf a,\mathbf b) \in \mathcal E^N$, satisfying \eqref{lem_FD_nontrivial_intersection}. We do so by first bounding the number of possible tuples $\mathbf a$ and then the number of possible tuples $\mathbf b$. For each $\mathbf a\in [M]^{J}$, the cylinder set $C(\mathbf a)$ has length 
\[
|C(\mathbf a)| \geqslant \frac1{2Q^{2(1+2\varepsilon)}},
\]
for the elements of $C(\mathbf a)$ are given by \eqref{alphaoft} for $t \in [0,1)$.
Hence, there exist at most
\begin{equation} \label{lem_FD_ub_cylinders_a}
2r\cdot 2Q^{2(1+2\varepsilon)}+1 \leqslant 4Q^{1+4\varepsilon} +1 \leqslant 5Q^{1+4\varepsilon}
\end{equation}
tuples $\mathbf a$ such that the cylinder set $C(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$ satisfies \eqref{lem_FD_nontrivial_intersection} for some $\mathbf b$.

Now for a fixed $\mathbf a= (a_1, \ldots, a_{J}) \in [M]^{J}$, we find an upper bound for the number of different $J$--tuples $\mathbf b\in \mathcal V_{J}(\mathbf a)$ such that $C(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$ satisfies \eqref{lem_FD_nontrivial_intersection}. Set $$\alpha=\alpha(\mathbf a) = [a_1,\ldots, a_{J}, M, M, \ldots].$$ 
For $\mathbf b = (b_1, \ldots, b_{J}) \in \mathcal V_{J}(\mathbf a)$,  let 
\[ n = n(\mathbf a,\mathbf b) =  b_{1}q_0(\alpha) + b_2q_1(\alpha) + \ldots + b_{J}q_{J-1}(\alpha) \]
be the integer whose digits in the  Ostrowski expansion~\eqref{Ostrowski_expansion_integers} with respect to $\alpha$ are the entries of $\mathbf b$. By Corollary~\ref{cor_nag},
if $(\alpha,\gamma) \in C(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$ then
\[
\|\gamma-n(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)\alpha\| < 4M/ q_{J}(\mathbf a). 
\]
This means that $\gamma$ belongs to an interval in $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ centred at $n(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)\alpha$ and of length at most $8 M/q_{J}(\mathbf a)$. Note from 
\eqref{useful} that if $\mathbf b_1, \mathbf b_2 \in \mathcal V_{J}(\mathbf a)$ then
\[
|n(\mathbf a,\mathbf b_1)-n(\mathbf a,\mathbf b_2)|
\leqslant 4M q_{J}(\mathbf a),
\]
so by \eqref{bad_lower_bound} the centres of the aforementioned intervals are separated by a distance of at least 
\begin{align*} \|n(\mathbf a,\mathbf b_1)\alpha-n(\mathbf a,\mathbf b_2)\alpha\| &\geqslant  (2(M+1)|n(\mathbf a,\mathbf b_1)-n(\mathbf a,\mathbf b_2)|)^{-1}\\  
& \geqslant \left(8M(M+1) q_{J}(\mathbf a)\right)^{-1}.
\end{align*}
Thus, any interval of length $2r$ can intersect at most
\[  
8M(M+1) Q^{1+2\varepsilon}\cdot 2r+2 \leqslant 16 (M+1)^2Q^{2\varepsilon}  
\]
intervals centred at points $n(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)\alpha$ of length at most $8 M q_{J}(\mathbf a)^{-1}$. We conclude that for a fixed $\mathbf a$, there are at most $16 (M+1)^2 Q^{2\varepsilon}$ values of $\mathbf b$ such that the set $C(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$ satisfies~\eqref{lem_FD_nontrivial_intersection}.

Combining the two bounds, we deduce that the number of sets $C(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$ that satisfy \eqref{lem_FD_nontrivial_intersection} is at most  
\[
5Q^{1+4\varepsilon}\cdot 16 (M+1)^2 Q^{2\varepsilon} = 80 (M+1)^2 Q^{1+6\varepsilon}.
\] 
For any such set the upper bound of Lemma~\ref{lem_size_of_cylinder_set}, together with~\eqref{T_m_is_large}, gives  
\begin{equation} \label{ub_nu_C}
\nu(C(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)) 
< Q^{(1+2\varepsilon)
	(1-2\kappa)}.
\end{equation}
Using~\eqref{ub_nu_C} together with the upper bound for the number of cylinder sets satisfying~\eqref{lem_FD_nontrivial_intersection}, we infer the upper bound
\[
\begin{aligned}
\nu\left(B_r(\mathbf x)\right) &< 80 (M+1)^2 Q^{1+6\varepsilon} \cdot  Q^{(1+2\varepsilon)(1-2\kappa)}  \\
&= 80 (M+1)^2 \cdot  Q^{2-2\kappa+4(2-\kappa)\varepsilon}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Using \eqref{r_level}, this results in the upper bound
\[        \nu\left(B_r(\mathbf x)\right) \leqslant 80 (M+1)^2 Q_0
r^{2\kappa-2-4(2-{\kappa})\varepsilon}.
\]

It is enough to prove the proposition for sets of the form  
\[
A=\{(\mathbf a,\mathbf b): \mathbf b \in \mathcal V_{J}(\mathbf a)\}
\]
for some $\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_{J})$; the result will then follow  by taking unions over words $\mathbf a \in [M]^{J}$.
Note from the definition of $\mathcal E_1$ that we have $\mathbf a \in \mathcal E_1^N$ if and only if $\bar{\mathbf a}\in \mathcal E_1^N.$ The result is trivially true when $\mathbf a\notin \mathcal E_1^N,$ as then $\nu(A) = \nu(\bar{A})=0.$ 

If $\mathbf a\in \mathcal E_1^N$ then, for $A$ as above, by the definition of ${\lambda}$ we have 
\[
{\lambda}^N(A) = \frac{c_{\lambda}^N |\mathcal V_{J}(\mathbf a)|}{T_m(\kappa)^{j_0 N}}\prod_{i=0}^{j_0 N-1}q_m\left(a_{im+1},\dots, a_{(i+1)m}\right)^{1-2\kappa}.        
\]
In light of the symmetry \eqref{q_k_inverse}, we similarly have
\[
{\lambda}^N(\bar{A}) = \frac{c_{\lambda}^N |\mathcal V_{J}(\bar{\mathbf a})|}{T_m(\kappa)^{j_0 N}}\prod_{i=0}^{j_0 N-1}q_m\left(a_{im+1},\dots, a_{(i+1)m}\right)^{1-2\kappa}.        
\]
By Lemma~\ref{vq}, we find that for every $\mathbf a\in\mathcal E_1^N$,
\[ |\mathcal V_{J}(\mathbf a)|\leqslant q_{J}(\mathbf a) \leqslant |\mathcal V_{J}(\mathbf a)|^{1+\frac{c}{R}} \quad \text{ and } \quad |\mathcal V_{J}(\bar{\mathbf a})| \leqslant q_{J}(\bar{\mathbf a}) \leqslant |\mathcal V_{J}(\bar{\mathbf a})|^{1+\frac{c}{R}}. \] 
By  \eqref{q_k_inverse} we have $q_{J}(\mathbf a) = q_{J}(\bar{\mathbf a})$ and therefore,  employing~\eqref{Qest}, we get
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\mathcal V_{J}(\mathbf a)| &\geqslant |\mathcal V_{J}(\bar{\mathbf a})|^{1/(1+\frac{c}{R})} = |\mathcal V_J(\bar{\mathbf a})| \cdot |\mathcal V_{J}(\bar{\mathbf a})|^{-c/(c+R)}\\ &\geqslant |\mathcal V_{J}(\bar{\mathbf a})| Q^{-(1+2\varepsilon)c/(R+c)}.\end{aligned} 
\]
This gives
\[ 
{\lambda}^N(A) \geqslant 
{\lambda}^N(\bar{A}) 
Q^{-(1+2\varepsilon)
c/(R+c)},
\]
and the other inequality follows by interchanging the roles of the sets $A$ and $\bar{A}.$

\label{ComparisonLemma}
Let $M_1, M_2 \in (0,\infty)$, let $F(t,u)$ be a $C^1$ function on $B = [0,1] \times [-1,1]$ such that
\[
\| F \|_\infty \leqslant 1,
\qquad 
\| \partial_t F\|_\infty \leqslant M_1, 
\qquad
\| \partial_u F \|_\infty \leqslant M_2,
\]
and put
\[
m_2 = \int_B |F(t,u)|^2 {\,{\rm d}} t {\,{\rm d}} u.
\]
Let $\nu$ be a probability measure on $B$, let $r > 0$, and denote by ${\Lambda}(r)$ the maximum of $\nu(\mathcal R)$ as $\mathcal R$ ranges over axis-parallel filled rectangles of respective side lengths $r/M_1$ and $r/M_2$ in $B$. Then
\[
\int_B |F(t,u)| {\,{\rm d}} \nu(t,u) \leqslant 
3r + {\Lambda}(r) \left(2 + \frac{M_1}r + \frac{2M_2}r + \frac{m_2 M_1 M_2}{r^4} \right).
\]

nodes.raw_latex:
Consider $\lfloor M_1/r \rfloor \cdot \lfloor 2 M_2/r \rfloor$ axis-parallel filled rectangles of respective side lengths $r/M_1$ and $r/M_2$, with non-overlapping interiors, whose union covers
\[
\left[0, 1 - \: \frac{r}{M_1}
\right] \times
\left[-1, 1 - \: \frac{r}{M_2}
\right].
\]
Let $N$ be the number of these filled rectangles $\mathcal R$ on which
\[
\max \{ |F(t,u)|: (t,u) \in \mathcal R \} \geqslant 3r.
\]
Within any such filled rectangle $\mathcal R$, there exists a pair $(t_0,u_0)$ such that $|F(t_0,u_0)| \geqslant 3r$. Thus, for any $(t,u) \in \mathcal R$, we have
\begin{align*}
|F(t,u)| 
&\geqslant |F(t_0,u_0)| - |F(t,u)-F(t,u_0)| - |F(t,u_0) - F(t_0,u_0)| \\
&\geqslant 3r - r - r = r,
\end{align*}
by the mean value theorem.
Therefore
\[ 
m_2 \geqslant N \frac{r^2}{M_1 M_2} r^2 = N \frac{r^4}{M_1M_2}.
\]
At most $\lceil M_1/r \rceil + \lceil 2M_2 / r \rceil$ filled rectangles, further to our original ones, are needed to cover $B$, so
\begin{align*}
\int_B |F(t,u)| {\,{\rm d}} \nu (t,u) &\leqslant 3r + (N + \lceil M_1/r \rceil + \lceil 2M_2 / r \rceil) {\Lambda}(r) 
\\ &\leqslant 3r + {\Lambda}(r) \left(2 + \frac{M_1}r + \frac{2M_2}r + \frac{m_2 M_1 M_2}{r^4} \right).
\end{align*}

By Lemmas \ref{lem_size_of_cylinder_set} and \ref{vq}, the innermost sum   satisfies
\begin{align*}
\sum_{\mathbf b\in \mathcal V_{KJ_0}(\mathbf a)}\!\!\lambda^K(\mathbf a,\mathbf b) 
&\leqslant 
| \mathcal V_{KJ_0}(\mathbf a)| \frac{2^K}{T_m(\kappa)^{j_0K}}Q_0^{(1+2\varepsilon)(1-2\kappa)K}\\
&\leqslant \frac{2^{K}Q_0^{(1-2{\kappa})(1+2\varepsilon)K+(1+2\varepsilon)K}}{T_m({\kappa})^{j_0K}}.
\end{align*}
This gives
\begin{align*}
(\lambda^K \times \lambda^K)(\mathcal D) &\leqslant \frac{2^{K}Q_0^{(1-2{\kappa})(1+2\varepsilon)K+(1+2\varepsilon)K}}{T_m({\kappa})^{j_0K}} \sum_{\mathbf a \in \mathcal E_1^{K}}  \sum_{\mathbf b\in \mathcal V_{KJ_0}(\mathbf a)}\!\!\lambda^K(\mathbf a,\mathbf b) \\
& = \frac{2^{K}Q_0^{(1-2{\kappa})(1+2\varepsilon)K+(1+2\varepsilon)K}}{T_m({\kappa})^{j_0K}},
\end{align*}   
where in the last step we have used the fact that $\lambda^K$ is a probability measure. The assumption \eqref{T_m_is_large} now yields 
\[   
(\lambda^K \times \lambda^K)(\mathcal D)  \leqslant  Q_0^{(1-2{\kappa})(1+2\varepsilon)K+(1+2\varepsilon)K}  
\]
and, recalling that $Q = Q_0^K$, we finally have
\[  
\int_{\mathcal D}\mathfrak J {\,{\rm d}} {\lambda}^{2K}  
\ll  Q^{2-2\kappa 
+ 4(1-\kappa)\varepsilon}.  
\]

First, note that
\[
{\lambda}^K\left(|s| \leqslant T\right)=\mathbb E\left(\chi_{|s| \leqslant T}\right),
\]
where $\chi_{|s| \leqslant T}$ is a characteristic function of the subset of $\mathcal E^K$ defined by the condition $|s| \leqslant T$. Then, by using the tower property of conditional expectation, we have
\[
\mathbb E\left(\chi_{|s| \leqslant T}\right)=\mathbb E\left(\mathbb E\left(\chi_{|s| \leqslant T}\mid \mathbf a\right)\right).
\]
We are going to upper bound the random variable $\mathbb E\left(\chi_{|s| \leqslant T}\mid \mathbf a\right)$, and then use the fact that an upper bound for a random variable is also an upper bound for its expectation.

To find a suitable upper bound for $\mathbb E\left(\chi_{|s| \leqslant T}\mid \mathbf a\right)$, we observe first that
\[
s = k_1 + k_2 N, \qquad N = \sum_{k=0}^{J-1} b_{k+1} q_k.
\]
Writing $\mathbf a = (\mathbf a^{(1)}, \ldots,\mathbf a^{(J/m)})$, the conditional probability that $N$ takes a specific value is at most $\prod_{i=1}^{J/m} |\mathcal V_m(\mathbf a^{(i)})|^{-1}$.  As $s \equiv k_1 \mmod |k_2|$, the conditional probability that $|s| \leqslant T$ is at most
\[
\mathbb E\left(\chi_{|s| \leqslant T}\mid \mathbf a\right) \leqslant \left( \frac{2T}{|k_2|} + 1 \right) \prod_{i=1}^{J/m} |\mathcal V_m(\mathbf a^{(i)})|^{-1}.
\]
By Lemma~\ref{vq} and the inequalities \eqref{R_is_large}, \eqref{Edef}, we infer that
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E\left(\chi_{|s| \leqslant T}\mid \mathbf a\right) &\leqslant \left(
\frac{2T}{|k_2|} + 1 \right)\frac{27^{J/R}} {\prod_{i=1}^{J/m}q_m(\mathbf a^{(i)})} \\
&\leqslant \left(
\frac{2T}{|k_2|} + 1 \right)\frac{27^{J/R}}{Q^{1-\varepsilon}}
\leqslant \left(
\frac{2T}{|k_2|} + 1 \right)Q^{2\varepsilon-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking expectations gives the conclusion of the lemma.

\label{ebc}
Let $(X,\ca{B},\mu)$ be a probability space, let $(f_n(x))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of non-negative $\mu$-measurable functions defined on $X$, and let $(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N} },\ (\phi_n)_{n  \in \mathbb{N}}$ be sequences of real numbers  such that
\[
0\leqslant f_n \leqslant \phi_n \qquad (n \in \mathbb N).
\]
Write
$$
\Phi(N)= \sum \limits_{n=1}^{N}\phi_n,
$$
and suppose that $\Phi(N) \to \infty$ as $N \to \infty$.
Suppose that, for arbitrary  $a,b \in \mathbb{N}$ with $a <  b$, we have
\begin{equation} \label{ebc_condition1}
\int_{X} \left(\sum_{n=a}^{b} \big( f_n(x) -  f_n \big) \right)^2\mathrm{d}\mu(x)\, \leqslant\,  C\!\sum_{n=a}^{b}\phi_n
\end{equation}

\noindent for an absolute constant $C>0$. Then, for any $\varepsilon>0$,  we have
\begin{equation} \label{ebc_conclusion}
\sum_{n=1}^N f_n(x)\, =\, \sum_{n=1}^{N}f_n\, +\, O\left(\Phi(N)^{\frac12}(\log(2+\Phi(N)))^{\frac{3}{2}+\varepsilon}+\max_{1\leqslant k\leqslant N}f_k\right)
\end{equation}
for $\mu$-almost all $x\in X$.

we define  
$\chi_{\delta}: [0,1) \to \mathbb R$ 
by   
\[
\chi_{\delta}(x):= \begin{cases}1 
\ \text{ if }  \ \|x\|\leqslant \delta  \\[1ex]
0 \ \text{ if } \  \|x\|>\delta,  \end{cases}   
\]
and its continuous upper and lower approximations 
$\chi_{\delta, \varepsilon}^\pm 
: [0,1)\to  \mathbb R$  
by
\[
\chi_{\delta, \varepsilon}^+(x):
= \begin{cases} 1 & \text{\  if   }  \  \|x\|\leqslant \delta \\[1ex]
1+ \dfrac{1}{\delta\varepsilon}(\delta-\|x\|) &\text{\   if }  \  \delta < \|x\| \leqslant (1+\varepsilon)\delta \\[1.3ex]
0 & \text{\ if } \  \|x\|>(1+\varepsilon)\delta \end{cases}
\]
and
$$   
\chi_{\delta, \varepsilon}^-(x)
= \begin{cases} 1 & \text{\  if } \  \|x\|\leqslant (1 -\varepsilon)\delta  \\[1ex]
\dfrac{1}{\delta\varepsilon}(\delta-\|x\|) &\text{\   if } \  (1-\varepsilon)\delta < \|x\| \leqslant \delta \\[1.3ex]

It follows from the definition~\eqref{def_cN} of the function $\mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi,N)$ that
\[
\mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi,N)\leqslant \mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\widetilde{\psi},N)\leqslant \mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi,N)+\mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi_{\tau},N)
\]
At the same time, it follows from~Theorem~\ref{mainCONV} that, for $\nu$-almost all pairs $({\alpha},{\gamma})$, we have $({\alpha}, {\gamma}) \notin \mathcal W(\psi_{\tau})$, which is equivalent to
\[
\mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi_{\tau},N)
\ll 1,
\]
Thus, $\nu$-almost surely,
\[
\mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\widetilde{\psi},N)=\mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi_{\tau},N) + O(1).
\]
For these pairs $(\alpha, {\gamma})$, when we change $\psi$ to $\widetilde{\psi}$, we modify the left-hand side of \eqref{countlacresult} by $O(1)$.
Similarly, using the notation $\widetilde{\Psi}:=\sum_{t \leqslant N} \widetilde{\psi}(n_t)$, we have
\[
\Psi(N)\leqslant\widetilde{\Psi}(N)\leqslant\Psi(N)+\sum_{t=1}^N\psi_{\tau}(n_t)=\Psi(N)+O(1),
\]
so by changing $\psi$ to $\widetilde{\psi}$ we modify the right-hand side of \eqref{countlacresult} by $O(1)$.
The term $O(1)$ is controlled by the error term in the right-hand side of \eqref{countlacresult}, so the claim is proved.

By using the upper bound \eqref{ub_mu_first}, and then \eqref{main_q_Harman_ub2}, \eqref{S_bound} and Proposition~\ref{prop_sum_S_m_n}  with
\begin{equation} \label{def_varepsilon_t}
\varepsilon_t =
\min\Bigg(2^{-\theta},\, \Big( \sum_{s=a}^{t}\psi(n_s) \Big)^{-\theta}\Bigg)
\qquad (a \leqslant t \leqslant b),
\end{equation}
we find
\begin{multline} \label{ub_sum_mu}
2 \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \nu(\mathcal E_{s}\cap \mathcal E_{t}) \leqslant
\mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b}
\Bigg(4(1+\varepsilon_s)(1+\varepsilon_t)\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t)+\frac{\psi(n_s)}{t^{A}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\,\\
+\, 
\frac{\psi(n_t)}{s^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}}
\, + \, \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}+T(s,t)\Bigg)\\
+ O\left(\mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} (n_s,n_t)\min\Big(\frac{\psi(n_s)}{n_s},\frac{\psi(n_t)}{n_t}\Big)\right).
\end{multline}
It follows from \eqref{def_varepsilon_t} that
\begin{equation} \label{epsilon_inverse_bound}
\varepsilon_t^{-1} \leqslant \max\left(2^{\theta},t^{\theta}\right) < 2t.
\end{equation}
Consequently $\sum\limits_{t=1}^{\infty}1/(t^{A}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}) <\infty,$ so we have the  upper bound
\begin{equation} \label{ub_first_two_terms}
\sum_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b}\left(\frac{\psi(n_t)}{s^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}} + \frac{\psi(n_s)}{t^{A}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\right)
\ll
\sum_{t=a}^b \psi(n_t)
\end{equation}
on part of the right-hand side of \eqref{ub_sum_mu}.

To bound the double sum $\sum\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} t^{-A}\varepsilon_s^{-1/2}\varepsilon_t^{-1/2}$ we consider two cases, according to whether $\sum\limits_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)>2$ or $\sum\limits_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)\leqslant 2$.

\noindent Case A: $\sum\limits_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)>2$.  In this case,
\[
\frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}
\leqslant
\frac{1}{t^{A}}\left(\sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r)\right)^{\theta},
\]
and so
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned} \label{sum_const_leq_linear_case1}
	\mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}} &\leqslant  \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}}\left(\sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r)\right)^{\theta} \\ &\ll \left(\sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r)\right)^{\theta}\leqslant \sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

\medskip

\noindent Case B: $\sum\limits_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)\leqslant 2$. In this case, we have $\varepsilon_t=2^{-\theta}$ ($a\leqslant t\leqslant b$), so
\[
\frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\ll\frac{1}{t^{A}}.
\]
Applying Corollary~\ref{cor_min_psi} with $\tau = A/2$, we may assume that
\[
\frac{1}{t^{A}}\leqslant\frac{\psi(n_t)}{t^{A/2}}
\qquad (t \in \mathbb N),
\]
whence
\begin{equation} 
\begin{aligned}
	\label{sum_const_leq_linear_case2}
	\mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}
		\varepsilon_t^{1/2}} &\ll \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} {\psi(n_t)}{t^{-A/2}} \\ &\leqslant \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} {\psi(n_t)}{s^{-A/2}}  \ll \sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
It follows from~\eqref{sum_const_leq_linear_case1} and~\eqref{sum_const_leq_linear_case2} that, in any case,
\begin{equation} \label{sum_const_leq_linear}
\mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\ll \sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t).
\end{equation}

We now proceed to estimate the first term on the right-hand side of~\eqref{ub_sum_mu}. To this end, we will make use of~\eqref{main_q_Harman_ub2}.  With this in mind, first note that by definition $t \mapsto \varepsilon_t$ is non-increasing, so 
\[
\varepsilon_t \psi(n_s) \psi(n_t)
\leqslant
\varepsilon_s \psi(n_s) \psi(n_t)
\]
whenever $s < t$. Moreover, we have $\varepsilon_t \leqslant 1$ for all $t\in\mathbb N$, and so 
\[
\varepsilon_s
\varepsilon_t
\psi(n_s) \psi(n_t) \leqslant \varepsilon_s
\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t).
\]
Thus
\begin{equation} \label{sum_eps_psipsi_developed}
4(1+\varepsilon_s)(1+\varepsilon_t)\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t) \, \leqslant \, 4\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t) + 12 \varepsilon_s \psi(n_s) \psi(n_t).
\end{equation}

We estimate the sum of the second term on the right-hand side of \eqref{sum_eps_psipsi_developed} by considering two cases, A and B as above.

\noindent Case A: $\sum\limits_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)\geqslant 2 $. In this case, we have
\begin{align}
\notag
&\mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \varepsilon_s\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t) \\
\notag
&= \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \psi(n_s)\psi(n_t)\ \min\Bigg(2^{-\theta}, \left(  \sum_{r=a}^{s}\psi(n_r)
\right)^{-\theta} \Bigg) \\ 
\notag
&\leqslant \
\max\Bigg(2^{1-\theta},\left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right)^{1-\theta}\Bigg)\mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b}\frac{\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t)}{\max\left(2, \sum_{r=a}^{s}\psi(n_r) \right)} \\
\label{ub_sum_eps_psipsi} &\leqslant 
\left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right)^{1-\theta}\sum_{a\leqslant t\leqslant b}\psi(n_t)\sum_{a\leqslant s\leqslant b} \frac{\psi(n_s)}{\max\left(2, \sum_{r=a}^{s}\psi(n_r) \right)}.
\end{align}
Applying \cite[Lemma~D2]{PVZZ2022} with 
\[
\gamma = 2,
\qquad
s_k = \psi(n_{k+a-1}),
\]
and $a,b$ replaced by $1,b-a+1$ respectively, gives
\begin{align*}
&\sum_{a\leqslant s\leqslant b} \frac{\psi(n_s)}{\max\left(2, \sum_{r=a}^{s}\psi(n_r) \right)} \\
&\qquad <
\frac32 + \frac{1}{2\log\frac32} \left(
\log \left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right) - \log \psi(n_a) \right).
\end{align*}
However, since we must be in Case (ii) or (iii) within the proof of that lemma, and since $\sum_{t=a}^b \psi(n_t) \geqslant 2$, we obtain
\[
\sum_{a\leqslant s\leqslant b} \frac{\psi(n_s)}{\max\left(2, \sum_{r=a}^{s}\psi(n_r) \right)} <
\frac32 + \frac{1}{2\log\frac32}\log \left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right).
\]
This, together with~\eqref{ub_sum_eps_psipsi}, implies that
\begin{align} 
\notag
&\mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \varepsilon_s\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t) \\
\notag
&\leqslant \left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right)^{1-\theta}\left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right)\left(\frac32 + \frac{1}{2\log\frac32} \log \left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right)\right)\\[2ex]
\label{ub_sum_eps_psipsi_2}
&\ll \ \left( \sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t)
\right)^{2-\theta}
\log^+ \left( \sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right).
\end{align}

\medskip

\noindent Case B:  $\sum\limits_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)<2$. In this case, we have
\begin{align}
\notag
\mathop{\sum\sum}
\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \varepsilon_s\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t)
&\leqslant \mathop{\sum\sum}
\limits_{a \leqslant s < t \leqslant b} \psi(n_s) \psi(n_t)
\leqslant \left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t)\right)^2 \\
\label{ub_sum_eps_psipsi_simple}
&< 2\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t).
\end{align}

Combining  \eqref{sum_eps_psipsi_developed},
\eqref{ub_sum_eps_psipsi_2} and \eqref{ub_sum_eps_psipsi_simple} gives
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned} \label{last_inequality}
	&\mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b}  (1+\varepsilon_s)(1+\varepsilon_t)\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t) \\ 
	&\leqslant  \left( \sum_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)\right)^2 
	+  O\left(\left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right)^{2-\theta}\log^+ \left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right)\right)
	\\ &\qquad + O\left( 
	\sum_{t=a}^b \psi(n_t)
	\right).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The result follows on combining
\eqref{ub_sum_mu}, \eqref{ub_first_two_terms}, \eqref{sum_const_leq_linear} and~\eqref{last_inequality}.

By employing Proposition~\ref{indiethm_general} with $\theta=2/3$, we find that it is enough to provide upper bounds for the sums
\begin{equation*}
\mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} (n_s,n_t)\min\Big(\frac{\psi(n_s)}{n_s},\frac{\psi(n_t)}{n_t}\Big)
\end{equation*}
and
\begin{equation} \label{sum_Tst}
\mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} T(s,t),
\end{equation}
where $T(s,t)$ is given by \eqref{def_S_prime}.
We now carry this out.

First, using the fact that $(n_t)_{t\in\mathbb N}$ is a lacunary sequence, we find
\begin{equation*} \label{ub_gcd}
\begin{aligned}
	\mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} (n_s,n_t)\min\Big(\frac{\psi(n_s)}{n_s},\frac{\psi(n_t)}{n_t}\Big)
	&\leqslant \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} n_s \frac{\psi(n_t)}{n_t}\\
	=\sum_{t=a+1}^b \psi(n_t)\sum_{a\leqslant s < t}\frac{n_s}{n_t}
	&\ll \sum_{t=a+1}^b \psi(n_t).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
Next, we are going to find a suitable upper bound for the sum~\eqref{sum_Tst}.

Recall that $T(s,t)$ is the sum of terms 
\[
\what{W}_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^{+}(kn_s,-k)\what{W}_{n_t,\varepsilon_t}^{+}(\ell n_t,-\ell)  \what{\nu}\left( -kn_s-\ell n_t,k+\ell\right),
\]
over non-zero integers $k,\ell$ for which
\begin{equation} \label{condition_T}
|k n_s-\ell n_t|< n_s^{1/2},
\end{equation}
where $\varepsilon_a, \ldots, \varepsilon_b$ are given by~\eqref{def_varepsilon_t}. By dividing both sides of~\eqref{condition_T} by $n_s$, we get
\begin{equation} \label{index_restriction_first_boundsv}
|k -\ell n_t/n_s|< 1.
\end{equation}


Hence, if $k$ and $\ell$ satisfy \eqref{index_restriction_first_boundsv} then they must have the same sign. Further, for each fixed integer $\ell$, there exists a set $S_{\ell}$ of at most two non-zero integers  $k$  satisfying \eqref{index_restriction_first_boundsv}.
On using the trivial bound  $|\what{\nu}(k_1,k_2)| \leqslant 1 $, it follows that
$$
|T(s,t)| \leqslant 2 \mathop{\mathop{\sum}_{ k, \ell \in \mathbb N} }_{k \in S_{\ell}} |\what{W}_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^{+}(k n_s,-k) \what{W}_{n_t,\varepsilon_t}^{+}(\ell n_t,-\ell) |.
$$

Note from \eqref{index_restriction_first_boundsv} and the inequality $\left|\ell n_t/n_s\right| > 1$ that
\begin{equation}
\label{ratio}
\frac12 \frac{n_s}{n_t}  k  \leqslant  \frac{n_s}{n_t} \max \{1,  k-1 \}  \, \leqslant \, \ell\, \leqslant \frac{n_s}{n_t} (k+1)\leqslant 2\frac{n_s}{n_t} k.
\end{equation}
Using \eqref{W_ub_psi} to bound $\what{W}_{n_t,\varepsilon_t}^{+}(\ell n_t,-\ell)$, and using \eqref{W_ub_psi}, \eqref{W_ub_1s2} and \eqref{ratio}
to bound  
$\what{W}_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^{+}(k n_s,-k) $, yields
\begin{eqnarray*}
|T(s,t)| &\ll  & \sum_{\ell  \in \mathbb{N} }
\ \min\left(\frac{n_s^2}{n_t^2}\cdot\frac{1}{\ell^2\psi(n_s)\varepsilon_s},\psi(n_s)\right)\psi(n_t)\\[2ex]
&\ll&
\sum_{\ell \leqslant \frac{n_s}{n_t\psi(n_s)\varepsilon_s^{1/2}}} \hspace{-5mm}
\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t) +
\sum_{\ell > \frac{n_s}{n_t\psi(n_s)\varepsilon_s^{1/2}}} \frac{n_s^2}{n_t^2}\cdot
\frac{\psi(n_t)}{\ell^2\psi(n_s)
	\varepsilon_s}\\[2ex]
&\ll&
\frac{n_s}{n_t}\frac{\psi(n_t)}{\varepsilon_s^{1/2}}  \leqslant \ \frac{n_s}{n_t}\frac{\psi(n_t)}{\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}. 
\end{eqnarray*}
The last inequality makes use of the fact that 
$t \mapsto \varepsilon_t$ is non-increasing.

By lacunarity, we have 
\[
\sum\limits_{1\leqslant s<t}n_s/n_t \ll 1.
\]
Consequently, if 
$a,b \in \mathbb{N}$ with 
$a <  b$, then
\[
\mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s < t\leqslant b} T(s,t)
\ll \sum_{t=a}^b\sum_{s=a}^{t-1}\frac{n_s}{n_t}\frac{\psi(n_t)}{\varepsilon_t^{1/2}} 
\ll \sum_{t=a}^{b}\frac{\psi(n_t)}{\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\, .
\]
Finally, recalling that the $\varepsilon_t$ are given by
\eqref{def_varepsilon_t}, we obtain the upper bound
\[
\mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s < t\leqslant b} T(s,t)  \ll
\left(\sum_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)\right)^{1+\theta/2}.
\]
The choice $\theta=2/3$ delivers \eqref{delta_set_frac23}.

nodes.raw_latex:
define an approximating function $\psi:\mathbb{N}\to [0,1]$ by setting $\psi(1)=0$ and 
\[ \psi(n) = \frac{1}{8 \log n} \qquad (n \geqslant 2). \]
Then, for $N\in\mathbb N$,
\[
\Psi(N)=\sum_{t=1}^N\psi(n_t)\asymp \log N.
\]

By Theorem~\ref{GeneralCountingThm}, there exists $\mathcal B_1 \subseteq \mathcal B$ of Hausdorff dimension $2$ such that, for all $(\beta,\delta)\in \mathcal B_1$ and all $t\in\mathbb N$, we have
\begin{equation} \label{GeneralMultThmQ_asymp_cN}
\mathcal N(\beta,\delta,\psi,t)\asymp\Psi(t)\asymp\log t.
